earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog refs for Impfondo/Bonjo are wordlists and Samarin 1984 (ethnicity); no grammar or phonology exists in the reference list

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid bonj1234 'Impfondo' (alt. Bonjo), and its reference list: Leitch 2009 (pp. 810-811), Gardner 1990, Campbell et al. 2022 (ElCat); Ethnologue/ELP/Wikipedia entries (Ethnologue 22nd ed. via the Internet Archive; ELP lang/521 via the Internet Archive; Wikipedia 'Bonjo language').
sources.note: Glottolog lists zero descriptive (grammar/phonology/sketch) references; ELP cites only Connell 2007, Austin 2008, Moseley 2010; Ethnologue gives classification C.143 Ngondi only; Wikipedia adds Maho 2009 NUGL (C143 Mbonzo). None says anything about stress or tone.

sources.citation: Gardner, William L. 1990 [2006]. Language use in the Epena district of Northern Congo. MA thesis, University of North Dakota; SIL Electronic Survey Report 2006-005. ix+146 pp. (108-page PDF).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Wordlist + sociolinguistic survey; an 'Impfondo' (Bonzo) 149-item wordlist is included, but p. 9 states that neither the author nor his colleagues recorded stress or tone on the wordlists and calls for a future phonological study 'including tone and stress'. No statement of where stress falls; no phonology section.

sources.citation: Leitch, Myles Francis. 2009. Language and dialect in Epena district south. Annales Aequatoria 30: 787-838.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic/dialect survey of Dibole (Babole). Bonjo/Impfondo appears only in classification remarks on pp. 810-811 ('Bomitaba has a much closer linguistic relationship with Bonjo of Impfondo, than to Dibole'). Nothing on Bonjo phonology, tone or stress; p. 827 notes survey transcriptions did not mark tone.

sources.citation: Annales Aequatoria vols. 21-29 (2000-2008), whole-volume open PDFs from aequatoria.be, a full-text search for stress/accent Bonjo/Bonzo/Mbonzo/Impfondo.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No article on Bonjo/Mbonzo; only an ethnographic reference to 'the Aka Pygmies and the Bonjo farmers' (2003) and a list item (2007). Nothing on the language.

sources.citation: Parker, Brian (SIL Congo). 2011-. Field materials on Mbonzo/Bonjo (Impfondo): 'Recordings in Mbonzo' (SIL LCA 54857) and any accompanying wordlist/phonology notes.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only known post-1990 primary fieldwork on the language; the archive entry is audio + photographs 'not available online', and any phonological write-up (e.g., an SIL Congo 'esquisse phonologique' or survey report) would supersede everything found here.

sources.citation: Connell, Bruce. 2007. Endangered languages in Central Africa. In Matthias Brenzinger (ed.), Language diversity endangered, 163-178. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter.

sources.note: The source ELP/Glottolog use for Bonjo's vitality; worth a look only to see whether it cites any description of Bonjo. Not a phonological source.

sources.citation: Leitch, Myles & Joseph Ndamba. 2005. The languages of Congo Brazzaville. In Keith Brown (ed.), Encyclopedia of Language and Linguistics, 2nd ed. Oxford: Elsevier.

sources.note: Country overview by the SIL Congo linguist who classified Bonjo; may name unpublished SIL Congo descriptions of Bonjo. Overview only, unlikely to state stress.

sources.citation: Bastin, Yvonne, A. Coupez & Michael Mann. 1999. Continuity and divergence in the Bantu languages: perspectives from a lexicostatistic study. Tervuren: MRAC, vi+225 pp. (Impfondo C10Ba2 and Mbonzo C31Mb wordlists.)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Holds the Tervuren 'Impfondo' and 'Mbonzo of Impfondo' wordlists (Glottolog language code tag); the Tervuren lists usually carry tone marks, which would at least establish the tone system, though no stress statement is expected.

sources.citation: CERDOTOLA / ACCT. 1987. Atlas linguistique de l'Afrique centrale (ALAC): Atlas linguistique du Congo. Inventaire préliminaire. Paris/Yaoundé: ACCT/CERDOTOLA. (Google Books ids eV7j-_mT_yYC, xAj7j6GEsTgC show 'Bonzo' + 'Likouala' hits.)

sources.note: Leitch 2009 identifies ALAC 1987 (with Jacquot 1971) as the only formal classification of these languages before the SIL surveys; ALAC notices sometimes include a short phonological/tonal sketch per language and would be the earliest place a note on Bonzo/Mbonzo tone could sit. Snippets not retrievable (Google search-inside blocked).
